answer: An agent marketplace commissions repairs to a marble terrace above a meadow. Job slots are drawn in proportion to collateral locked for the entire review window, not the number of agent accounts. A bond cannot back two simultaneous slots, and random post-storm inspections slash it for false completion. Splitting one budget among aliases leaves the same total draw weight; an attacker needs more capital locked and real repair capacity to gain more slots. Rich operators can still dominate, and inspectors may collude, so cap exposure per verified operator and rotate auditors.
